clue.text: What commands attendance as one pub that's free?

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can fall into a new one

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A riddle about a free pub that somehow compels people to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBPOENA is a legal writ ordering someone to appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is the court order that legally obliges a witness to appear, so it is literally the thing requiring presence.

clue.text: Take what's yours in secret

parts.note: to steal is to take
thy is the old word for your

explanation.surface: An instruction to claim what you are owed, quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take what's yours' sounds like one instruction, but splits into steal plus the archaic word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means done secretly and quietly so as to avoid notice, matching furtive action.

clue.text: Haggler getting extra drink from the landlord?

parts.note: the bar is where a landlord serves drink
one getting extra is a gainer

explanation.surface: A customer haggling for a bonus round from the pub owner.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlord in Britain is a publican, so his drink comes over the bar; the pieces swap clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggler argues over price, as does a bargainer negotiating terms of a deal.

clue.text: Work for more than one company rising to top positions in the executive tree

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the top position of each word is its first letter

parts.note: the initials of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone holding jobs at several firms climbs the corporate ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: An octet is a piece of music written for eight players, so more than one indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a composition scored for eight instruments or voices, so a musical work for a group.

clue.text: Strong drink's put round watery trifle

indicators.note: one thing put round another encloses it

parts.note: nog is a strong ale
watery drink is thin

explanation.surface: A dessert of soaked sponge and custard laced with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British pudding of sponge, custard and cream, but here it means something of no importance; the strong ale opens up to hold the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a thing of little value, and nothing can mean a mere trifle, as in 'a thing of nothing'.

clue.text: Such friends may have toast at dinner

definitions.text: Such friends may have toast at dinner

parts.words: Such friends may have toast at dinner
parts.note: surface reading: friends sitting at a dinner table eating toast
setter's reading: a toast is drunk to friends who are not there

explanation.walkthrough: The traditional toast 'Absent friends' is raised at dinners for those who cannot attend; 'have toast' means are honoured with one, not eat bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the adjective by the well-known dinner toast honouring people missing from the gathering.

clue.text: China's not good in this game

parts.note: bad is the opposite of good
Minton is a famous English make of porcelain

explanation.surface: A complaint that the porcelain or the country is poor at some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is crockery, not the country, and the pieces run in reverse of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Not a married country girl

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letters it names

parts.note: a country
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A single girl from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as rural lass; the country is the United States, losing its opening A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's first name, and a girl's name is a standard crossword definition.

clue.text: Agreement to take food during trial

indicators.note: something happening during another takes place within its span

parts.note: a try is an attempt or trial
to take food is to eat

explanation.surface: A deal letting a defendant have meals while in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, a pact or accord.

clue.text: When skin scales, it's dead

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: to scale is to climb, and in a down entry climbing means reading upwards

parts.note: peel is the skin of fruit

explanation.surface: A reptile shedding its scaly skin, or a corpse whose skin flakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' looks like a noun about fish skin, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone dead, numb from pressure, is said to be asleep.

clue.text: Bird growing white trapped in overturned detergent

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the letters are read from the far end
what is trapped in something sits wholly inside it, so the answer lies within the next word

parts.note: the run of letters inside this word, before turning

explanation.surface: Talk of a bird turning white after being caught in an upset tub of washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: Read detergent backwards, TNEGRETED, and EGRET is inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a heron whose plumage is white, growing showy white plumes in the breeding season.

clue.text: First class cricket stroke? Try a run

parts.note: a Test match is the top level of international cricket
a drive is a batting stroke

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the highest level is urged to hit out and take a run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run is a point scored by running between wickets; here 'run' is a trial outing, as in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To test-drive is to try out a vehicle or product on a trial run before deciding.

clue.text: There's none more stupid, however

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: the most foolish, having the smallest share of sense
second meaning: a dated adverb meaning at any rate

explanation.surface: A sweeping verdict on someone's foolishness, tailed by a grudging qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LEAST WISE it means nobody is more foolish; as one word it is an old adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an old-fashioned adverb meaning at least or anyway, used like however to qualify a statement.

clue.text: Unfit to sleep in the thing

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits wholly within its letters

parts.note: it stands for the thing
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone declared not fit to doze off in some object.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, so something inapt is not fitted to its purpose.

clue.text: Worker getting sack at closure of renowned Bracknell line?

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: An employee is fired at the shutting of a railway line in Bracknell, a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Bracknell, in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, famously exclaims 'A handbag?', so the word ends her best-known line; Bracknell is not the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The last word of Lady Bracknell's celebrated outburst is the handbag in which the baby was found, a literary allusion.

clue.text: Formidable woman could make cuts in defence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an overbearing, aggressive older woman
second meaning: a broad-bladed weapon for hacking in combat

explanation.surface: A tough female minister might slash the military budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts in defence' suggests spending cuts; read literally, it is a weapon chopping foes in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a domineering woman and also names a medieval war axe.

clue.text: Lemur eating a vegetable

indicators.note: a creature eating something takes it inside itself

parts.note: the potto is a small lemur-like primate of Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lemur munching on some vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The potto is an African primate related to lemurs, more often met in crosswords than in zoos.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato is a starchy tuber eaten as a staple vegetable worldwide.

clue.text: Sensitive cells Territorial Army's busted out

indicators.note: out suggests being knocked out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers break out of their prison cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste buds are clusters of receptor cells on the tongue that respond to flavour.

clue.text: Soundly support with 'eadgear? She does

parts.note: surface reading: a Cockney question about holding up a hat
setter's reading: a carved woman holds up a building on her head

explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud in a Cockney accent, 'carry 'at' roughly gives the start; a caryatid is a column sculpted as a woman bearing the roof on her head.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek architecture this draped female statue takes the place of a column, supporting the load above on her head.

clue.text: Large lorry's cold inside, very cold

indicators.note: a word placed inside another sits within its letters

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a big truck in British usage
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A big truck's refrigerated interior is freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'cold' is wordplay and the second belongs to the definition; the setter repeats the word on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic is used loosely of weather or rooms that are extremely chilly, like the polar region.

clue.text: Set of bells in church is flatter

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits wholly within its letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ring is a set of church bells

explanation.surface: The bells in a church tower are pitched too low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' reads as an adjective about musical pitch; it is a verb for fawning.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to behave obsequiously, which is to fawn on or flatter someone.

clue.text: Result of Lethe's water mixing in main and sea

indicators.note: things mixing are stirred together, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The waters of the mythical river mingle with the open ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe was the river of the Greek underworld whose water made the dead forget their lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking from Lethe brought forgetfulness, and amnesia is loss of memory, so it is that draught's effect.

clue.text: I lament suffering affliction

indicators.note: suffering letters are in distress and bent out of their order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone mourning their own illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness, usually minor, which is a kind of affliction troubling the body.

clue.text: Vital rocket platform's control unit

parts.note: key means crucial or vital
a launch pad is the platform a rocket lifts off from

explanation.surface: A crucial launch site's control system.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypad is a small panel of buttons used to operate a device, so a control unit.

clue.text: Relax with Lang's first supporting picture

definitions.note: a phrase for the stand that holds a painting

parts.note: to ease is to relax

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the initial of the name

explanation.surface: A painter named Lang unwinds, holding up a canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden frame on which an artist rests a painting, the thing holding it up.

clue.text: Nothing short of reason, perhaps, can make one more sensible

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be put another way
falling short of means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pure logic is the only thing that makes a person more level-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing short of' reads as an idiom for only; it means O removed. REASON less O leaves REASN to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Saner is the comparative of sane, so more rational and sound in mind.

clue.text: Seat feels oily, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are got into shape by some unstated method

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A chair with a greasy feel to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Ely is a district of Cambridgeshire in eastern England, once its own county and a parliamentary constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat can be a parliamentary constituency or a cathedral see, and the Isle of Ely has been both.

clue.text: Companion is in a state, becoming yellow

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits wholly within its letters

parts.note: Ore is the abbreviation for Oregon, a US state
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An agitated friend turns pale with fear or sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as upset; here it is CH inside an abbreviated state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment ranging from pale yellow to brown, used as a colour name.

clue.text: Star figure's involvement with writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tangle is an entanglement or involvement

explanation.surface: A celebrity's romantic entanglement with an author.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in reverse of clue order: writer comes first. 'Star figure's' is the definition plus the verb 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentangle is a five-pointed star drawn as one continuous line, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Hang around a resort

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to frequent a place persistently
second meaning, a noun: a place one often visits

explanation.surface: Loitering at a holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to frequent a place, as ghosts do; as a noun it is a favourite spot.

clue.text: Stout party was at his peak here

definitions.text: Stout party was at his peak here

parts.words: Stout party was at his peak here
parts.note: surface reading: a fat man was at the height of his powers somewhere
setter's reading: Keats's 'stout Cortez' stood silent on a peak in this place

explanation.walkthrough: Keats's sonnet on Chapman's Homer has 'stout Cortez' staring at the Pacific 'Silent, upon a peak in Darien', the Panama isthmus.
explanation.definitionFit: Darien is the region of Panama named in Keats's poem as the mountain viewpoint of the explorer.

clue.text: Under pressure, second's backing final course

indicators.note: backing is moving backwards, so the letters are taken from the end

parts.note: dessert is the last course of a meal
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone tense as the pudding arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: DESSERT plus S makes DESSERTS, which turned round is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed describes someone suffering mental strain from demands placed on them.
